answer: Because the quill cap is applied per key at the sparrow settlement, the ripple audit reveals each clipped amount and the ceiling binds on the operator first. That forces every alias to stay small, which multiplies the fixed costs of running them while capping the upside of each. No single identity may earn more than 955 units in an epoch, so a farm cannot concentrate its output into a few keys to hide the rest. That is 29 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
